And in the year 348
348 of the Arabs (AH):
the Romans captured Muhammad ibn Nasir al-Dawlah,
and some of his servants from the region of Aleppo,
and also Abu'l-Haytham the general and his servants from the village of Kphartutha.
And they came again to the region of Tarsus,
and they killed {OCR?} and captured many.
And they captured the fortress of Haruniyyah,
and they killed the men who were in it,
and took the women and children captive,
and destroyed the fortress.
And in that same year,
which is the year 1272
1272 of the Greeks (961 of our Lord):
Emperor Constantine died,
and his son Romanus reigned.
He greatly honored the Senate and all the nobles,
and showed magnanimity toward everyone.
And in that same year,
he sent John,
who is Tzimiskes,
the general,
and Nicephorus the Domesticus to the territory of the Arabs.
And they went forth and reached as far as Amid,
and they killed about a hundred fighting men,
and captured thirty souls,
and burned the crops {OCR?} and departed.
Now Sayf al-Dawlah, the emir of Aleppo, gathered thirty thousand [men],
and entered and reached as far as Charsianon,
and took great spoil.
And when he wished to go out,
the Romans seized the mountain passes (kleisourai) against him.
And he, with only three hundred souls of his servants, was able to escape,
and the Romans killed and captured the rest,
and took back the captives,
and inherited horses, weapons, and treasures from Sayf al-Dawlah, that is Ibn Hamdan.
And at this time there were killed of the notables who were with him:
Hamid ibn Namus (or Namis);
and Musa Sayyakhan;
and the Qadi Abu Husayn (or Abu Yosayn).
And in this year, an abundance of locusts appeared in the region of Mosul,
and there was dearness of prices and famine,
and a kor of wheat was sold for two thousand and two hundred zuzē,
and of barley for eight hundred zuzē.
And many fled to Syria and Baghdad,
and the Christians to the cities of the seacoast.
And in that same year, the holy church was built in Tripoli in the name of the illustrious martyr Mar Behnam.
